source_text:
πατήρ·" ἵνα νοῇς οὕτως· εἰ καὶ κέκληται πρὸς υἱοθεσίαν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ υἱὸς
ἀνεδείχθη νέος, ἀλλὰ μὴ ζητείτω τὰ ὑπὲρ φύσιν, μηδὲ ἀξιούτω μαθεῖν ἅπερ μηδὲ
thought_title: The veiled saying means even an adopted son must not seek what is beyond nature
orientation: Cyril is explaining the veiled force of Christ's saying from Matthew 24:36, addressing what the disciples should understand from it.
pass_a_gloss: Father; so that you understand thus: even if the human being has been called to adoption and has been shown to be a new son by adoption, yet let him not seek the things beyond nature, nor let him think it right to learn what not even

choices.why: The glossary fixes 'adoption' for υἱοθεσία, avoiding the banned 'adoption as sons' and 'sonship'.
The glossary fixes 'beyond nature' for this phrase, avoiding 'above nature' and 'supernatural'.

choices.english: has been shown to be a new son
choices.why: ἀναδείκνυμι means to show forth or display; the passive with νέος conveys that the human being has been publicly displayed as a new son, matching Cyril's point about renewed humanity.

choices.english: let him think it right to learn
choices.why: ἀξιόω with infinitive means to deem worthy or think fit; the third-person imperative keeps the hortatory force of the Greek.
rejected: let him be worthy to learn

pass_b_english: He said that only the Father knows. Understand it this way: even if a human being has been called to adoption and has been shown to be a new son, he must not seek what is beyond nature, nor think it right to learn what not even [text breaks off]

last_rejected.why: 'νέος' modifies the person, not 'son'; means 'shown to be a new person/renewed', not 'new son'.
last_rejected.fix: shown to be a new son, or a son renewed
last_rejected.ruling: νέος can modify υἱὸς naturally; 'new son' is within normal Greek word-order range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Third-person imperative 'let him not seek' softened to 'must not seek'; changes grammatical force.
last_rejected.ruling: μὴ ζητείτω (3rd sg. imperative) rendered 'must not seek' preserves prohibition; 'let him not' vs 'must not' is preference.

last_rejected.why: Third-person imperative 'let him not deem it fitting' softened to 'nor think it right'; changes grammatical force.
last_rejected.fix: nor let him deem it fitting
last_rejected.ruling: μηδὲ ἀξιούτω (3rd sg. imperative) rendered 'nor think it right' preserves prohibition; 'let him not deem' vs 'must not' is preference.
